text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Dennis Rose QC, a former chief counsel to the Federal Attorney-General, says the Coalition's controversial superannuation surcharge is illegal and open to a High Court challenge. If his legal opinion is upheld, the Federal Government could face a A$1.5 bllion Budget hole. Page 1.

As the July 1 deadline for telecommunications deregulation gets closer, communications companies are stepping up their efforts for a stake in a national telecommunications market worth A$18.6 billion a year, with the planned release of a A$140 million-plus tidal wave of advertising, marketing and sponsorship. Optus and Telstra have already earmarked approximately A$120 million for mainstream media campaigns. Page 1.

Despite continued opposition to the Federal Government's work-for-the-dole scheme from welfare groups such as the Brotherhood of St Laurence, Labor and the Australian Democrats yesterday dropped their strong opposition to the controversial proposal, a move which should see the plan approved in the Senate. Page 3.

Dominant New South Wales right faction, the ALP national executive, is likely to intervene in two preselections in its New South Wales branch in a bid to prevent the State ALP office from becoming involved in the rank-and-file preselection system, except when there is no sitting member. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday unveiled the Federal Government's work-for-the-dole schemes, which aim to force welfare recipients to return services to the community. The Coalition has committed A$15 million to create 10,000 positions under the scheme, which will cover 18 to 24-year-olds who have been unemployed for at least six months. Page 1.

British author Graham Swift has denied claims by University of Queensland Professor of English John Frow that his 1996 Booker Prize winner, Last Orders, contains striking yet unacknowledged debts to the 1930 William Faulkner classic, As I Lay Dying. Page 1.

Despite legal advice from Dennis Rose QC, a former chief general counsel to the Attorney-General's Department, who says the controversial A$500 million-a-year Budget superannuation tax is unconstitutional, Prime Minister John Howard yesterday said he would press ahead with the tax, which would affect the super of about 330,000 high income earners. Page 1.

The Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission yesterday ordered the Royal Women's Hospital and the Freemasons Hospital to pay A$26,000 to three women, who were all in heterosexual defacto relationships, for following Victorian law and refusing to give them access to IVF treatment because they were unmarried. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Under the first such revenue-raising plan in Australia, Central Queensland University is offering international students, who pay up to A$40,000 for a degree, free holidays to Ayers Rock and the Whitsundays, free computers and free textbooks if they manage to get friends or family members to enrol. Page 1.

According to a breakdown of the latest Health Department hospital waiting list figures, hospital waiting lists in Sydney's west and south are increasing at an alarming rate, supporting claims by hospital administrators in those areas that they are suffering an unequal proportion of the growing burden on the health system. Waiting lists for major hospitals in the city's north and east have shrunk. Page 1.

Following the release of a study by the Council of Deans of Education into the quality of teacher education, Federal Schools Minister David Kemp yesterday blamed "fashionable" teaching for low literacy levels among Australian children. The report has angered teachers which blamed them for their students' poor results. Page 3.

After Federal Cabinet yesterday gave its approval for legislation to be introduced into Parliament next week to implement key parts of the Howard Government's controversial work-for-the-dole scheme, which will target young people who have been out of work for extended periods, Vocational Education and Training Minister David Kemp said the Government would retain the right to force some unemployed people to become involved. Page 3.
THE AGE

In an escalation of the public transport dispute, the Victorian Government has responded to the weekend's 48-hour strike by transport unions by endorsing an all-out assault on the union movement, including speeding up the sale of trains and trams and the possible use of powerful anti-strike laws. The plan has been approved by State Cabinet. Page 1.

Following a decision by Federal Human Rights Commissioner Antonia Kohl, who found that three women in de facto relationships were discriminated against by the Royal Women's and Freemasons' Hospitals because they were refused IVF treatment, the Victorian Government yesterday pledged to review its ban on de facto couples using the fertilisation technique. Page 1.

According to a study by the National Centre for Research into the Prevention of Drug Abuse which found that 61 per cent of the 511 Western Australian drug-using respondents had injected less than once a day and 24 per cent had injected less than once a week in the month before the survey, many intravenous drug users are more likely to be ordinary full-time workers with families than addicts. Page A3.

Ringwood Magistrates Court was told yesterday Jamie Warwick Hall, of Mossman Drive, Heidelberg, a convicted sex offender accused of stalking two school girls, believed he was in turn the victim of stalking by police. Hall was denied bail on the grounds he posed an unacceptable threat to the community. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
